newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish coalition agrees on new ministers.
newsitem.headline: Polish coalition agrees on new ministers.

text.p: Poland's two ruling leftist coalition parties have agreed on candidates to head two new key ministries, to be created on January 1 under a cabinet reorganisation, a senior coalition official said on Friday.
"The prime minister should soon ask the president to appoint new ministers. The candidates will soon be known," Aleksander Bentkowski, a leader of the Polish Peasant Party (PSL), told Reuters.
The two new powerful portfolios, which will embrace four current ones, are the ministry of interior affairs and administration and the economy ministry.
Under a coalition agreement in October, candidates to head the two ministries will be put forward by the Peasants' larger coalition partner, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD).
A coalition source, who asked not be named, said that Wieslaw Kaczmarek -- a former liberal privatisation minister, now a deputy treasury minister -- will become economy minister.
The economy minister will be in charge of drafting the government's industrial and foreign trade policies.

The source said the SLD's influential cabinet chief-of-staff Leszek Miller will be proposed as the interior and administration minister, although President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who has some say over the post, may object and propose his own candidate.
The coalition still has to find a candidate for the labour minister, a portfolio vacant since Andrzej Baczkowski died last month. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
